resolvedFindings.description: The initial disabling implementation accepted a hold entry whose reason was missing, empty or whitespace, because it checked only (quest ID, field) membership. This violated the documented-hold guard.
resolvedFindings.suggestedFix: Require a nonblank string reason for every None override and add regressions for missing, empty and whitespace reasons.
resolvedFindings.resolution: Root added hold_reasons lookup and isinstance(reason, str) plus reason.strip() validation. The independent reviewer inspected the final diff and reran the full suite successfully.
evidence: work/afternoon-2026-11-14/hold-reason-before.log: three expected failing subtests before correction

reviewNotes: The None override path requires a previously nonnull field, a matching heldFields entry with a nonblank reason, and the exact prior Myanmar text SHA-256. The existing duplicate override guard remains before mutation.

validate_fields still requires matching source and review record sets, English title identity, exact English and Myanmar field hashes, and a nonempty held English proposal. Missing or stale source/review hashes do not bypass validation.

The correction pack contains no drafts or rows and changes only 5639.detail to null. The retained legacy English and machine proposal are explicitly held evidence; they do not enable a current source state.

EXPECTED_DISABLED_FIELDS is constructed exclusively from composed reviewed None overrides and passed to Lua as a table. The 5639 old-release assertion remains active when no reviewed disabling is present. The new real-bridge regression checks held-offer fallback/capture while retaining title and completion.
Git diff/status inspection found no historical translation pack changes. Final composed rows, including English aliases, are identical between 1.2.7 and 1.2.8.
The final builder docstring uses an actual line break rather than a literal backslash-n.

No native proofreading or live-client verification was performed or inferred from this code review. The new 1.2.8 build, package validation and publication remain the root release workflow's next gates.
